title: Gujarat Clears ₹1,600 Crore Investment Across 23 Industrial Units
shortDescription: A high-level committee chaired by Deputy CM Harsh Sanghvi approved eligibility certificates worth ₹1,600 crore for 23 industrial units, expected to create about 5,634 jobs.
genZNote: Two schemes, one committee, one Deputy CM's name — Industrial Policy-2015 handled the ₹770 crore chunk, Atmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme-2022 handled the rest.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: On 1 April 2026, a high-level committee chaired by Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghvi approved final eligibility certificates extending financial assistance to 23 major industrial units across the state.

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: Under Industrial Policy-2015 (Incentives to Industries): ₹770.29 crore approved across 22 large units.
Under Atmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme-2022: ₹837.67 crore approved for a major unit in Panchmahal district.
Combined approvals expected to generate approximately 5,634 employment opportunities.
Incentive framework covers net SGST reimbursements, interest subsidies, and EPF reimbursements.
District-wise highlights: ₹186.77 crore (auto, Ahmedabad); ₹148.34 crore (textile/paper, Surat); ₹81.09 crore (metal/minerals, Gandhinagar).

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: This is a concrete example of Gujarat's industrial-incentive architecture (Industrial Policy-2015 and Atmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme-2022) actually disbursing approvals, connecting Gujarat's economic-policy GK to a dated, numbers-backed 2026 event.

highYieldFacts: ₹1,600 crore across 23 units, ~5,634 jobs, chaired by Deputy CM Harsh Sanghvi.
commonTraps: Attributing the full ₹1,600 crore to a single scheme rather than splitting it between the two named schemes.
